old_problem: Both Procedure and Criteria are TBD, and earlier reviews did not establish whether Display off(default) meant OS power management, physical-display activity telemetry, vGPU policy or NVIDIA board display mode. DeepSeek proposed nvidia-smi/GUI behavior without a documented mutation path. A wrong interpretation can blank the only console; an actual NVIDIA Display Mode Selector write updates board firmware, may affect all adapters if no index is given and requires a reboot, so generic confirmation/revert language was not enough.
disposition_reason: Resolve Engineering Decision Pending and BLOCKED using NVIDIA's authoritative Display Mode Selector documentation and the three adjacent independent Items: Display off(default), Scalable visualization and Display enabled align with the vendor's `physical_display_disabled`, `physical_display_enabled_8GB_bar1` and `physical_display_enabled_256MB_bar1` states. NVIDIA identifies A40/L20/L40/L40S as factory-default physical-display-disabled boards with 64GB BAR1 and provides the exact supported tool syntax. This supplies the missing standard semantics and Expected Result without inventing OEM behavior. Exact GPU identity, supported/certified platform, pinned tool package, current/final state, maintenance/reboot and recovery remain runtime/project gates. A state-changing firmware write is used only when the approved test requires transition; a default-state check must preserve the as-found state. Classification becomes REQUIRES because execution may update GPU firmware and reboot but the safe contract is now complete.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1777, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 blocked record, original pending/blocked analyses, exact-code search, adjacent independent rows 1778 and 1779, and ED rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was directly opened as Functionality row 1778 / Wistron-HW-00411-V002 / 9f93367f19c3d4a6.

The adjacent Items form the same three states named by NVIDIA: default Display off, Scalable visualization and Display enabled. They remain separate Source Keys and coverage identities under ED-02/ED-20, but the vendor terminology resolves the state model for this row.

NVIDIA's tool guide defines `physical_display_disabled` as physical display ports disabled with 64GB BAR1 for vGPU/compute use and lists A40, L20, L40 and L40S with that default. Other listed workstation/RTX boards default to enabled 256MB BAR1, so applicability/default status is model-specific and must be proven rather than guessed.

NVIDIA documents `displaymodeselector --gpumode <mode_name> [-i num]`; omitting the index can switch every eligible board. The review therefore requires one exact serial/BDF/tool index and prohibits an unscoped all-adapter invocation.

The utility updates board firmware, warns of permanent unusability on incompatible/uncertified systems and requires reboot after applying a mode. ED-07/ED-29 principles therefore require immediate approval, stable power, exact activation, pre/post mode/BAR1/PCIe/driver evidence and no automatic retry.

NVML/nvidia-smi Display Active telemetry reports whether a monitor is attached; it is not the board firmware display-mode oracle. Acceptance must use the pinned vendor tool/workflow plus post-reboot BAR1/physical-port behavior and identity correlation.

For an as-supplied default verification, changing the board first would destroy the evidence: capture and judge the as-found mode. Only an explicitly approved transition branch may write `physical_display_disabled`, and its evidence must be labeled configured-mode rather than factory-default proof.
No Display Mode Selector invocation, firmware write, reboot, display change, log clear or other DUT action was executed.

test_case.test_name: NVIDIA Display Mode — physical display disabled default
test_case.purpose: For an exact supported NVIDIA GPU and OEM-qualified platform, verify the board's Display off(default) state as `physical_display_disabled` with the vendor-defined BAR1/display behavior, or—only under a separately approved transition branch—set that state on one selected adapter, activate it by the required reboot and verify complete GPU/host recovery.
required_package: Exact SUT and GPU model/SKU/serial/UUID/PCI BDF plus Display Mode Selector adapter index; vendor table proving the model supports switching and whether its factory default is physical-display-disabled
OEM/vGPU platform certification or explicit OEM approval for the exact board/system/mode; project ruling whether this execution is an as-found default check or a state-transition test
NVIDIA-authorized, hash/version-pinned Display Mode Selector package compatible with the board VBIOS/driver/OS; current and target mode/BAR1 ledger
Dedicated maintenance window, workload/VM/display drain, stable power, independent non-GPU console/SSH/BMC, reboot approval, signed recovery/default-mode artifact and vendor/OEM service path
Pre/post GPU identity, VBIOS, PCIe, BAR1, driver, display-port, workload and OS/BMC event collector with visual evidence when physical no-output behavior is part of the approved criterion
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED; firmware/reboot approval required for transition. First bind the exact GPU by serial/UUID/BDF and tool index, prove model/tool/OEM support, record current board mode through the approved vendor workflow, `nvidia-smi -q` BAR1/identity, PCIe link, driver/workloads, display path and preserved events. For the factory-default branch, make no mode write: verify the untouched supported A40/L20/L40/L40S board reports the vendor-defined physical-display-disabled/64GB-BAR1 state and expected absence of accelerated physical display output. For an owner-approved transition branch only, drain all users, obtain immediate confirmation and invoke the pinned vendor command for exactly one adapter: `displaymodeselector --gpumode physical_display_disabled -i <VERIFIED_INDEX>`; capture full output once, then perform the required approved reboot and verify OFF/boot/OS-ready timeline, active target mode, BAR1, PCIe/GPU/driver/workload health and display behavior. Restore only if the signed final-state plan says so. Never omit `-i`, use nvidia-smi display-active as the mode oracle, clear logs, retry a firmware write or reboot automatically.
test_case.expected_result: The exact supported target is unambiguously identified and the applicable vendor default/target is `physical_display_disabled`; for A40/L20/L40/L40S default verification the untouched as-found state matches physical display ports disabled with the vendor-defined 64GB BAR1. If the approved transition branch is used, one scoped tool write succeeds, the required reboot activates the same mode, physical accelerated output is disabled as defined, BAR1/mode evidence matches and the same GPU returns with healthy VBIOS, PCIe link, driver, workloads and no new unexplained OS/BMC/GPU errors. No other adapter changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires model/OEM/tool applicability, exact one-GPU identity, authoritative active-mode and BAR1 evidence, expected physical-port behavior, no unintended adapter change, full reboot/recovery health and preserved logs. An as-found default PASS additionally requires no prior write in this execution and a vendor model whose default is display-off. Unsupported/unlisted hardware is N/A only with authoritative model documentation; missing support is BLOCKED, not N/A. Display Active alone, blank output alone, tool exit without post-reboot activation, unscoped all-GPU action, wrong/default-enabled model, mode/BAR1 mismatch, GPU/PCIe/driver loss or recovery failure is not PASS and is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Do not run the tool unless exact model, VBIOS, OEM-certified platform, pinned package and target mode are compatible; vendor warns misuse can permanently render the GPU/system unusable.
Bind serial/UUID/BDF to the Display Mode Selector index immediately before action and always scope `-i <VERIFIED_INDEX>`; omission can update all switchable boards.

Treat mode transition as GPU firmware write plus reboot: require stable power, drained workloads/VMs/display sessions, independent non-target console, immediate approval, full output and a signed recovery artifact/service path.
Do not confuse nvidia-smi/NVML monitor-connected telemetry with firmware display mode; require active-mode/BAR1 and physical-behavior correlation after reboot.
Stop on identity, compatibility, tool, write, reboot, PCIe, GPU, driver, display or evidence anomaly. Do not retry, write another mode, reset, reboot or power-cycle automatically.
expected_evidence: Source Key/Variant, as-found-default versus transition branch, model default/applicability reference, OEM qualification, SUT/GPU serial/UUID/BDF/index and tool/VBIOS/driver hashes/versions
Complete pre-state board mode/BAR1, PCIe/GPU/driver/workload/display identity, preserved logs, maintenance/stable-power/reboot approval and recovery readiness
For transition only: exact single-adapter command plus untruncated stdout/stderr/exit status and no-retry/no-other-adapter audit
Approved reboot/OS-ready timeline and post-reboot active mode, 64GB BAR1, physical-port behavior, GPU/PCIe/driver/workload/OS/BMC health and visual evidence where applicable
Final approved state, any recovery action and engineer-owned PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/N/A verdict with authoritative N/A proof
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity, unsupported combination, tool warning/error, incomplete write, reboot failure, missing GPU, PCIe/driver fault or lost display/management access, stop and preserve tool, EEPROM/mode, VBIOS, console and event evidence. Do not rerun the selector or cycle modes. Use the independent console/BMC and vendor/OEM-approved board recovery or signed default-mode restoration procedure under owner direction; escalate to vendor board service if the GPU/system is not healthy.
